utterances.text: The only question I want to ask is in relation to what Mr. Stanisic said about all respect for their dignity and their soldierly honour. Did you see during that month Mr. Stanisic display any other attitude towards the UN hostages?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, never. He regarded them as members of the United Nations who had been deployed there to exercise the duties conferred upon them in that peacekeeping operation. He viewed them primarily as members of the armies of their respective countries who found themselves in a position where they were viewed by the entire world chained to posts without their uniforms, and he expressed his intention to have them released and taken back to their respective units to do what they we were sent there to do under full military gear and therefore he regarded them as soldiers who were performing their military duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And may we have 1D05248 on screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And it's with regard to paragraph 43 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, can I ask one clarifying question. In relation to your last answer, witness, you said Mr. Stanisic viewed them primarily as members of the armies of their respective countries. Does that mean that he did not view them as members of the United Nations forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I misspoke. They were members of the military formations of their countries but were deployed on an honourable mission as representatives of the international community bound by the orders and decisions of the United Nations. He regarded them as such and not as foreign soldiers in an alien territory. They were there to introduce peace and not as occupying forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although his last words were that he would -- let me check that carefully. He said: "... and hand you over to your United Nations command, that is to say, representatives of your governments." I'm trying to understand what that addition means, apparently not handing them over to the United Nations command but to representatives of their government. And that also in relation to your -- that part of your answer, that he viewed them primarily as members of the armies of their respective countries.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When he said representatives of governments, I believe that Mr. Stanisic primarily had in mind representatives of embassies of certain countries who were there as well. That's how I understood the additional part where he mentions representatives of governments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jordash. I'm also looking at the clock. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I've probably got about 10 to 15 minutes left. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. I'm also looking at Mr. Stanisic. He might prefer a break at this moment or would Mr. Stanisic prefer the 10 or 15 remaining minutes and then have a break and then have another 45 minutes for the last?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A break would be preferable. Then we first take a break, we resume at 6.00 and we expect you to finish by 6.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's just finish in the next 10 to 15 minutes, Mr. Dragicevic, and then I'll sit down for others to question you. The document on the screen you deal with at paragraph 43 of your statement and you say there that you visited Pale for the last time in early July of 1995 and handed over this message; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Were you present when President Chirac and Chirkin [phoen] provided that message?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you discuss the message then with Mr. Stanisic? Where did you come by the information that this had come from -- directly from those two?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I learned it from Mr. Stanisic on our way to Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Were you there when it was read out by Karadzic's spokesman, Samotica [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: As far as you are aware, did the Contact Group plan and the negotiations resume following the resolution of the hostage crisis?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's precisely what the message is about, i.e., that the resumption of peace negotiations with the Contact Group would be agreed to as the starting position with an addition to the effect that the VRS should open up all the roads for unhindered passage of humanitarian convoys.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, just returning to the subject of Mr. Stanisic's speech and view concerning whether the hostages were UN personnel or representatives of their respective countries, are you able to testify as to whether Mr. Stanisic received any award from the United Nations themselves?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I'm truly not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. But you are aware that he received awards from, as we see from your statement, the French; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He received a medal from the head of the French intelligence service, Mr. Dewatre.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Were you there at that point in time when he received the medal?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was on an official visit to Paris and the French intelligence service together with Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the purpose of that visit?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think the visit came about primarily thanks to the role Mr. Stanisic played in having the UN personnel hostages released because most of the UN personnel were French. At the same time, specific conditions were put in place for co-operation between the DGSE, the French intelligence service, and DST, the French counter-intelligence service, since both these services had common priorities. When I say "common priorities" I mean first of all fight against radical Islam and terrorism in general.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could all unnecessary microphones please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me just ask you about paragraph 56 of your statement, D466, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: While that's coming up on the screen, you make the comment there that the SDB of Serbia had better relations with the US, French, and Chinese services than with the services of the RSK and the RS. Which period are you referring to when you make that comment?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I meant the period shortly before the hostage crisis.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Then moving on to paragraph 65, and whilst that's coming up, could you just explain why you came to the conclusion or what was your source of information concerning the fact that the SDB of Serbia had better relations with the foreign services than those in Croatia and Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: For the simple reason that most of the contacts were maintained with these services rather than those from Croatia or Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, at paragraph 65 you mention briefly there the SDB of Serbia helping to establish a check-point in the Republika Srpska. When was that and what was the check-point? Perhaps I should say what was the check-point? What assistance was given and what was the nature of the check-point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Continue, Mr. Witness, with your account, but with using numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Should I repeat what I said? In 1996, Number 11 paid a visit and the main subject of discussion was the protection of international forces, the IFOR, in Bosnia, as well as an active participation in the overall protection of these forces in 1996 and 1997. In order for this to come to fruition, the SDB of Serbia helped establish a specific check-point of that agency in Republika Srpska, or a specific point from where they would be able to more effectively cover the area in co-operation with our service.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was anybody on the -- sorry, let me start that again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I think the witness mainly repeated what is already in the statement and therefore what you specifically asked, what assistance was given, that's already in the statement, unless you had something else on your mind, the witness repeated that, and then what was the nature of the check-point. Could you tell us what the nature of the check-point was and also answer the first question, when it was in 1996 that 11 visited Belgrade? Perhaps first the last question. A month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't recall the month. I know it was in 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any season? Spring, summer? If you don't remember --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was summer already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Summer 1996. And then what was the check-point exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't tell you anything specific about the point because I visited the location only once. I didn't go there again because the nature of my work did not take me there. I didn't have anything to do with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What exactly was checked at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I can't answer the question because I simply didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did this have anything to do with Number 10?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, number 10 was present there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know in which capacity he was there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I think he was the official leader of that group for Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I just ask you about two other things, very quick things.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: First of all, could we have on the screen 1D05247, and it's a document which records a visit to the USA intelligence community, Belgrade, 7th of March, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you recall this visit?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have page 17 -- 16, I beg your pardon, of the English. Not sure of the B/C/S. Let's go to the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The bit I'm interested in is the assessment of the -- of the visit, taking into consideration all elements of the visit of the RDB delegation to the US intelligence community. Then if we can go over the page to 17 where it says in the first paragraph, first complete paragraph -- let me read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ask for page 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, 17, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have page 8 in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Me too. Can we go to page 17, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [As read] "It is important to reiterate that Number 11 did not receive the delegation of Croatian security services despite the state of their bilateral relations." Were you aware of that fact, Mr. Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely as you put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Finally, let's go, if we can, to 1D05076.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And it's the -- this should be a -- do you recognise the document, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And it's document coming from the embassy of SFRY in Washington and it's a response to the delegation visit to Washington, and there you can see in the first full paragraph it notes that: [As read] "The USA estimates that the Serbian DB is very solid and professional service that successfully copes with the left and right extremism and it has the function of carrying out peaceful politics." And further down the page at the second to last paragraph we have a repeat of that, and also the additional: "The DB has the function of carrying out the implementation of DS and peaceful politics of the president and the Serbian authority." Were you aware of the following before you testified today of that view held in 1996 by the US?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I think that this was the first visit by a group from the State Security Service to the US. Earlier we said that there had been quite a few obstacles and suspicions with regard to our visit, but in the course of our talks with our counter-parts from the agency, we reached some vital conclusions that contributed and created a new bilateral political dimension, but it happened, as they put it, step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we also have an answer to the question. The question was whether you knew about this view before you testified today? The view held in 1996 by the US? Were you aware of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have seen this document before I came to this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you see it for the first time? Was in The Hague that you ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, the first time I saw it in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps I can clear this up, Your Honour, with another document which answers this, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, after 25 minutes which is not 10 to 15 minutes, Mr. Jordash, and of course, I wonder, if this view is expressed in a document, have you ever discussed with the Prosecution to tender this as a bar table document, saying it illustrates how the co-operation was appreciated by the US, instead of asking a witness where you know that he has seen this document only now whether he was aware, he says, well, I've seen it this week. I mean, we were not here to teach -- to educate witnesses, but rather to hear evidence. But if there's only one document that would be the last and then we --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Hopefully. I should have shown this document, the next one, instead of that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Show the right documents to the right witness, I would suggest. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: 1D02596, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, if you just have a look at this document, and see if you recognise it.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise this document. In the upper right corner, you can see my name and you can see the signature of Mr. Jovica Stanisic. Whenever he read a document, he would designate it to a certain person and here you can see this document bears my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you saw this at the time?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I had it in my files.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Last paragraph says that inter alia: [As read] "...CIA and NSC evaluate their co-operation with SDB is of utmost importance for the implementation of the Dayton Accords and preservation of safety of American soldiers." Was that a view you had heard at the time?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the view came from?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: These views were expressed personally by Number 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, no further questions. Thank you, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now I see you said the signature of Mr. Stanisic was here. Has he signed for Mr. Nadazdin or did I ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the Chef de Cabinet of the foreign minister, Mr. Vlado Nadazdin, sent this document to Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... oh, you mean that the signature is the initials at the top under your name, is that the -- I'm just trying to find that's where we find Mr. Stanisic's initials?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you are absolutely right. You can see my names and then the initials, yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The initials of Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I give now an opportunity to the Simatovic Defence, Mr. Petrovic, to cross-examine you. Mr. Petrovic, are you ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good evening Mr. Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I have a few questions only for you on behalf of Mr. Stanisic's [as interpreted] Defence. First of all, let us clarify one thing that you talked about a while ago with my colleague Jordash --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know whether it was only a mistake in the translation or the transcription, but I take it that you are asking questions on behalf of Mr. Simatovic, his Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yes, of course. I think I said as much and it must have been a mistake in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, a while ago when you spoke with Mr. Jordash about the year 1996 and the establishing of a point in Republika Srpska, in the translation that we have, we have the term "check-point" appearing. Would you agree with me that this was actually an intelligence point that was set up by this American agency in Republika Srpska rather than a check-point of sorts in a specific location?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the word "check" in itself implies something being checked. Therefore, I would agree with the first part of your question that it was an intelligence point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dragicevic. Hopefully this is clear now. Mr. Dragicevic, judging by your statement it seems that you were for a period of time the special advisor to the chief of the department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that according to the job classification in the state security department, there were six positions of special advisors to the chief of the department?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I really cannot confirm that. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that there were more than one special advisor?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there were several of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It is true that each of those special advisors had his own domain from the scope of responsibility of the department?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, each of them had their specific duties and responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that a special advisor was not permitted to become directly involved of the work of the chiefs of administration in the state security department?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you tell us if you know when and how the 9th Administration was formed of which you became a head at a certain point in time?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: The 9th Administration was set up as an administration for international co-operation. I was at its head and initially I was the only member of the staff of that administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when the administration was set up and how on the basis of which document, if you know, of course?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know on the basis of which document, but I know that it happened in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If you don't know on the basis of which document it was set up, do you know then who was it whether it be an individual or an organ who adopted such a document to serve as the basis?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the chief of the department is directly responsible for such issues. It is his decision which is then forwarded to competent organs who issue proper decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, for a long time you worked at the service and your appointment to the position of the head of the department from the position of a special advisor, can we qualify it as promotion or is it stagnation or what kind of a career move was that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I never considered that to be degradation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can we then understand it to be a promotion?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was a special advisor and head of the administration at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dragicevic. Let us first go back to something that you mentioned today when you answered the questions by my learned friend, Mr. Jordash. You spoke about the exchange of information with various services, notably that of the US, Russia and others. I'm interested in hearing whether that was the exchange of intelligence information that your department had acquired?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So are we talking about the information and data that were mainly obtained by the 2nd Administration of the department?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness. Mr. Dragicevic, in your statement, which is D466, in paragraph 80 when you spoke about Mr. Simatovic you mentioned that Simatovic was the head of a section that was dealing with foreign countries. Do you perhaps know whether this refers to a section in the Belgrade AOS centre that was dealing with the American intelligence service? In other words, are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If you know, can you please tell us what kind of section are we talking about? What is this AOS section doing?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: That is a section that is dealing with the American service.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us specifically in what sense, with the American service agents or those who were working on the ground? Can you give us a description of what they operated on?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: They were mainly involved in counter-intelligence work covering possible activities of the American service in the territory of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the speakers please pause between questions and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, could you also please make a small pause between question and answer, otherwise the interpreters have difficulties in following. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was AOS dealing with American citizens who were, for whatever reason, of interest for the service without knowing whether they were, indeed, members of the American security service or not?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know any specifics but it is quite natural that in the course of counter-intelligence activities you have to focus on other people as well, not only members of the intelligence agencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, just a few more questions. Do you know that Mr. Stanisic -- sorry, Mr. Simatovic, in May 1993 was appointed special advisor to the chief of the department? Were you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I really cannot confirm that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, do you know that Mr. Simatovic had never been appointed chief of the 2nd Administration in the department?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you use the acronym AOS and at least I do not find it in paragraph 80. Could you briefly tell me what you refer to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour. In paragraph 80 the witness states that Simatovic was the chief of a department and he dealt with western countries. I put to the witness that this was AOS, that the title of the department Mr. Simatovic worked for was AOS. This is not contained in the statement, rather there is just a vague sentence that I wanted to clarify with the witness. And AOS is short for American intelligence service, in Serbian, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The last line would have answered my question, Mr. Petrovic. I just wanted to know what it was, AOS. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, one more question. A moment ago you said that when the 9th Administration was formed, you were there as the only staff member. How long did it take for the administration to be structured in terms of personnel and work?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I was there on my own for about a year. After that I tried to find individuals who would be suited to do the job. The main obstacle lay in the lack of knowledge of foreign languages because using interpreters in day-to-day communications proved risky at times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please focus on the question. How long did it take for that administration to be operational as far as personnel and work is concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me repeat that I was there on my own for a year and it took me another two years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, were precisely these personnel issues the reason why for awhile you were both a special advisor and head of the 9th Administration? In other words, you seem to be wearing two hats whereas in fact you only performed one of these two roles; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Dragicevic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Farr, is it you who will cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Farr. Mr. Farr is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Good evening, Mr. Dragicevic. Can you hear me clearly?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Good evening. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: To start with, can you please tell us when you first became aware of the existence of a DB special unit?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I learned of the existence of a DB special unit in 1995 when preparations were underway for such a unit to be set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you tell us specifically when in 1995 and how you became aware that a unit was being set up?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I think it was in late 1995. I learned about it from my colleagues who were there with me. I don't know how else to describe it to you. I wasn't able to find out anything in specific -- anything specific since I wasn't involved in these duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In paragraph 76 of your statement you indicated that you never discussed the JSO or any other unit with Mr. Stanisic. Did you ever discuss the JSO or any other DB unit with Mr. Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Neither with Mr. Simatovic, nor with Mr. Stanisic. Let me repeat, our duties and tasks were strictly defined.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did you ever have any information that led you to believe that Mr. Simatovic was a member of the DB special unit?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: As far as you know, did the DB special unit exist at the time of the hostage crisis in May and June of 1995?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, the special unit was set up in 1996. Everything that happened before that period were preparations to establish the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: What was the name of the unit at the time you learned about it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: It was not a proper unit as yet. There were preparations to set up a unit that was to be called a unit for special operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So you were only ever aware of the unit under the name unit for special operations or JSO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And who do you know to have been the commander of that unit?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the JSO unit was Mr. Milorad Lukovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to turn to your work history now. In paragraph 2 of your statement you say in 1990 you became the head of administration for international co-operation of the federal service. And you go on to say that according to the rules then in force, only the federal service was entitled to maintain contacts with foreign services and that republic services could not do that. Is it correct that this changed with respect to Serbia from a legal standpoint in approximately November 1992 with the issuance of rules amending the rules on the internal organisation of the State Security Service and from that time on the Serbian DB could maintain, legally, contacts with foreign services?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: At paragraph 3 of your statement you describe your trip to the London Conference with Kertes and you indicate that you were fired from the federal service by Minister Bulatovic upon your return. Is it correct that the London Conference occurred in August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I can't state with any certainty which month it was in 1992, but I was there with Mr. Kertes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You say in the same paragraph, and you told us earlier that the reason you were fired is that you -- well, the reason given for your dismissal was that you hadn't sought permission from the minister. Is that the only reason that you were dismissed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't try to investigate if that was the only reason or not. I was officially informed that I was supposed to seek permission from the federal minister for my trip to London with Mr. Kertes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Were there any public allegations against you of misconduct while you were attending the London Conference that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: What were the allegations?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: The allegations were published by the media to the effect that as a professional I accompanied Mr. Kertes to London --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that you want to intervene or object.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, no, neither, I do apologise. May Mr. Stanisic be excused for two minutes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, we have only 10 minutes left --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please. Please continue your answer, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The media stated that I accompanied Mr. Kertes to London as a professional who had the task of placing wire-taps or bugs, listening devices into the conference room, the room where the conference was held.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: As far as you know, did those allegations have any role in your dismissal?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: They may have been used to that end but they could not have had anything to do with it. What was at play was a total anarchy or dissolution within the federal service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you the following, Mr. Dragicevic: Earlier you were asked whether not having the permission to go to London was the only reason, you say "I didn't try to investigate it." You also testified that there was no -- it was not required to seek the permission, you were not aware of any rule. Now, if I'm fired on having done something which is not against the rules, I would immediately ask myself is that the real reason. Now, apparently you are telling us now about allegations, et cetera, et cetera, I would have expected you to include that in the first answer whether there were any other than the formal reasons, you told us this was the formal reason, apparently that you thought that there may have been other matters, I would have expected you answering the question in accordance with the whole truth, to immediately raise that issue and say it was published or in the media it was said that, and apparently you have thought about that as a possible reason for being fired. You may proceed, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, what's your response to those allegations that you've just described?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I was not given any sort of opportunity to respond to these allegations or to appeal the decision that the federal service issued me with.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: What I am asking is what is your response today? Do you say that these allegations were true, do you say they were false?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: The allegations were completely untrue. I'm a person who studied the English language and literature as well as law and I have no propensity for anything electronic or any interest in it, so these allegations were quite ridiculous. And if I may add, to manage to place listening devices in a conference room which, as we all know full well, is always screened for anything of the sort prior to the opening of the conference, is quite strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Moving on to your new job at the Serbian DB, in paragraph 4 of your witness statement you indicated that you knew Mr. Stanisic "from before." How did you know Mr. Stanisic from before?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic became employed in the State Security Service of the Republic of Serbia a year after my employment there started and we knew each other even from before that period.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We know each other from that period, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And when was that period exactly?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: That was 1975 when I started working in the State Security Service of the Republic of Serbia. After a certain period, I took up studying law at the university in Belgrade. I was studying part-time and the service banned me from continuing my studies there. I was very unhappy with IT and I left the service in 1979.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Stanisic on a continuous basis from 1975 until the time he gave you the job in 1991 or 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: When I left the service in 1979 I became the manager of the publishing house called the Yugoslav Review and then I would see Mr. Stanisic after that on occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that you remained friends during that period?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: In my view a person can be considered lucky and happy if he or she has one or two friends and Mr. Stanisic was to me a colleague with whom I used to work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, I am looking at the clock, we are two minutes away from adjournment. Would this be a suitable moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I have one matter to be put on the record before we adjourn, which is the following: That 65 ter document 6291 tendered by the Prosecution on the 20th of October, 2011, and admitted provisionally under seal was by mistake assigned number P3039, a number which was already assigned on that same day to document 65 ter 6301. Therefore, now 65 ter 6291 has been assigned in e-court number P3042. This is hereby on the record. Mr. Jordash, the list of names with the numbers is uploaded in e-court I do understand. Could we perhaps tomorrow in the event that you tendered documents and I think there are a lot which may not have been tendered, I'm not quite certain, I rather not do it now, it being 7.00 and caring about my reputation with the interpreters, transcribers, et cetera, but first thing tomorrow morning if you prepare it well, it will not take much time. Then, Mr. Dragicevic, I would like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone or communicate in any other way with anyone about your testimony, whether that's testimony you've given today or whether that's testimony still to be given tomorrow. And when I say tomorrow, Mr. Farr, could you give us an estimate on how much time you really would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, my initial estimate is 4 hours. Of course I'm conscious that the Chamber always pays careful attention to the way in which things proceed, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you could shorten that, of course, without loss of quality, that of course would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00 because we adjourn until Wednesday, the 9th of November at 9.00 in the morning in this same Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 9th day of November, 2011 at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.
